chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Mu'amar ibn Khallad, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:
I said to him, 'What are the people reporting regarding eating clay and its abhorrence?' So he said: 'Rather, that is the wet [clay], and that is the loam [soil].'
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between wet clay and loam in Shia jurisprudence regarding eating?
ai.summary: Imam Al-Reza (peace be upon him) clarifies the distinction between the types of clay mentioned in reports regarding eating, explaining that the 'abhorrent' clay refers to wet clay (al-mabluul), while the permissible or distinct type is loam (al-madar). This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the Shia scholarly approach to resolving apparent contradictions in narrations by specifying the physical state of the substance, thereby distinguishing between general prohibition and specific conditions. It underscores the importance of contextual interpretation in fiqh, where the texture and moisture content determine the ruling on consumption.

en.hubeali:
Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Moamar Bin Khallad, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, said,
‘I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘What are the people reporting regarding eating the clay and its abhorrence?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘But rather, that is the wet and the loam’.
en.sarwar: 7. Ahmad ibn Muhammad has narrated from Mu’ammar ibn Khallad who has said the following: “I once asked abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,
about what people narrate as regards eating clay and that it is undesirable. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is clay and chunks of dirt.’”
